statusLegend.absent: key/value not read by this tag; silently ignored (DecodeJSONConfig does not disallow unknown fields)
statusLegend.deprecated: read (or migrated) with a warning; still loads
statusLegend.rejected: Build() (or handler start-up, where the detail says so) errors and the config does not load/start
statusLegend.constraintItems: for kind=constraint the status describes what happens to a config that violates the constraint in that tag

perVersionKeysNote: Lists keys a tag reads without error (accepted or deprecated). Keys that are rejected (kcp header/seed before v26.9.9, tls verifyPeerCertInNames in v26.3.27, allowInsecure=true) or silently ignored (kcp header/seed in v26.9.9) are left out; see items. finalmask internals are covered by the finalmask findings.

items.detail: Case-insensitive; omitted means raw (tcp); raw=tcp, xhttp=splithttp, kcp=mkcp, ws=websocket are aliases; any unknown name fails the load with 'unknown transport protocol'.
HTTP/2-3 transport is a removed feature in all three tags (PrintRemovedFeatureError pointing to XHTTP stream-one H2/H3), so the config does not load.
QUIC transport is a removed feature in all three tags (points to XHTTP stream-one H3); the config does not load.
These networks still load in all three tags but log a non-removal deprecation warning recommending XHTTP.
New alias of network in v26.7.28 with the same values; when both keys are present method wins; v26.3.27 silently ignores it, so a config that uses only method falls back to raw there.
Case-insensitive; empty equals none; xtls is a removed feature and any other string fails with 'Unknown security'.
Legacy XTLS is rejected in all three tags (migrate to flow xtls-rprx-vision with tls or reality).
REALITY is only accepted with network raw/tcp, xhttp/splithttp or grpc; ws, httpupgrade, kcp and hysteria fail the load.
security reality without a realitySettings object fails the load; security tls without tlsSettings is fine (an empty TLS config is used).

Every transport settings object present is built even when network selects a different transport, so an invalid leftover object (e.g. kcpSettings with seed next to network ws) still fails the load; editors should drop settings of unselected transports.
rawSettings and tcpSettings are the same object; if both are present rawSettings wins and tcpSettings is discarded.
xhttpSettings and splithttpSettings are the same object; if both are present xhttpSettings wins.
A header object must carry a type key (lower-cased); a missing or unknown type fails the load; http takes request/response objects.

v26.7.28 renamed sessionPlacement to sessionIDPlacement (values path|cookie|header|query, default path) with no migration: the old key is silently ignored from v26.7.28 and the new key is silently ignored by v26.3.27, so the wrong spelling silently falls back to path.
Old spelling, only read by v26.3.27 (path|cookie|header|query; any other value fails the load there); ignored without warning afterwards.
v26.7.28 renamed sessionKey to sessionIDKey (default x_session for cookie/query, X-Session for header); the old key is silently ignored afterwards.
Old spelling, only read by v26.3.27; silently ignored from v26.7.28.

New in v26.7.28: a predefined table name (ALPHABET, Alphabet, BASE36, Base62, HEX, alphabet, base36, hex, number) or a custom ASCII-only character set; when set, sessionIDLength.from must be > 0 and table-size^length must give at least 2^31 combinations, otherwise the load fails.
New in v26.7.28 (integer or 'from-to' string); only used together with sessionIDTable, otherwise a UUID session ID is generated and the length is ignored.
Empty means auto; any other value fails the load.
Empty means queryInHeader; any other value fails the load.
Empty means repeat-x; any other value fails the load.
Empty means auto; cookie and header are only allowed in mode packet-up; query/path and anything else fail the load.
Empty means path; any other value fails the load.
Upper-cased, default POST; GET is only allowed in mode packet-up.
A Host entry in headers (any case) fails the load; use the host field.
If set, both ends of the range must be > 0 (padding cannot be disabled).
maxConnections and maxConcurrency are mutually exclusive (both with a non-zero upper bound fails the load).

Default changed when xmux is omitted or all-zero: v26.3.27 uses maxConcurrency 1, v26.7.28+ use maxConnections 3 (hMaxRequestTimes 600-900 and hMaxReusableSecs 1800-3000 unchanged); write it explicitly to get the same behaviour on every core.
downloadSettings (a nested streamSettings object) is not allowed in mode stream-one.

When extra is present the whole xhttp config is re-read from it and only host, path and mode are kept from the outer object, so every other outer key (including downloadSettings) is silently discarded.

Int32Range fields (xPaddingBytes, uplinkChunkSize, scMaxEachPostBytes, scMinPostsIntervalMs, scStreamUpServerSecs, sessionIDLength and the xmux ranges) accept only an integer or a 'from-to' string; an object fails to unmarshal.

v26.3.27 and v26.7.28 fail the load on any header value with a removed-feature error pointing to finalmask udp masks (header-*, mkcp-original, mkcp-aes128gcm; v26.7.28+ also offer mkcp-legacy {header,value}); v26.9.9 still declares the key but dropped the check and never reads it, so it is silently ignored and the obfuscation is simply lost.

Same as header: a removed-feature error in v26.3.27 and v26.7.28 (migrate to finalmask udp mkcp-aes128gcm or mkcp-legacy), silently ignored in v26.9.9, which means a v26.9.9 node with seed talks plain mKCP and will not interoperate with a seeded peer.
Boolean congestion control flag, removed from the struct and proto in v26.7.28 (silently ignored afterwards).
Decoded by v26.3.27 but never used by its kcp core (GetReadBufferSize is commented out); gone from v26.7.28.

v26.7.28 replaced writeBufferSize (megabytes, 0 meaning 512 KB, default 2 MB) with maxSendingWindow in bytes (default 2097152); it must be at least mtu or the load fails, and the old key is silently ignored.
Only read by v26.3.27 (megabytes); silently ignored from v26.7.28, where maxSendingWindow (bytes) replaces it.
New in v26.7.28, default 1; values below 1 fail the load.
Allowed range tightened from 10-5000 ms (v26.3.27) to 10-1000 ms (v26.7.28+); default 50; out-of-range fails the load.
v26.3.27 has no MTU check (commented out); v26.7.28+ fail the load when mtu < 21; default 1350.
Whenever hysteriaSettings is present, version must be exactly 2 or the load fails.
0 (default 60) or 2-600 seconds; anything else fails the load.

Already inert in v26.3.27/v26.7.28 (decoded, a warning says it moved to finalmask.quicParams, value never used); removed from the struct in v26.9.9 and silently ignored; use finalmask.quicParams.congestion (reno|bbr|brutal|force-brutal).
Warned-and-ignored in v26.3.27/v26.7.28, silently ignored in v26.9.9; the replacement is finalmask.quicParams.brutalUp (bandwidth string, >= 65536 B/s when set).
Warned-and-ignored in v26.3.27/v26.7.28, silently ignored in v26.9.9; the replacement is finalmask.quicParams.brutalDown.

Warned-and-ignored in v26.3.27/v26.7.28 (whose replacement is finalmask.quicParams.udpHop {ports, interval}); v26.9.9 removes both the transport key and quicParams.udpHop and moves port hopping to a finalmask udp mask of type udphop.
New in v26.9.9: with masquerade type proxy, adds X-Forwarded-* headers to the proxied request.
Empty or 404 serves Not Found; any other value is not caught by Build() but makes the inbound fail when it starts listening.
From v26.7.28 a hysteria inbound or outbound refuses to start unless its streamSettings network is hysteria ('not hysteria transport'); v26.3.27 does not check.
The hysteria transport only listens/dials with security tls ('tls config is nil' otherwise); not caught by Build(), so an inbound fails at startup and an outbound at first dial.

true fails the load with a removed-feature error pointing to pinnedPeerCertSha256/verifyPeerCertByName; in v26.3.27 this is clock-gated (before 2026-06-01 UTC it only warned and still skipped verification, after that date it is rejected); false is harmless in every tag.
Comma-separated names the peer certificate must match; it replaced verifyPeerCertInNames (a string array), which v26.3.27 rejects and later tags silently ignore.
v26.3.27 fails the load on any non-null value; v26.7.28 dropped the key, so it is silently ignored and no name check is applied.
Only v26.3.27 reads it (other values fail the load there); removed from struct and proto in v26.7.28 and silently ignored.
Lower-cased; empty means chrome; unsafe is allowed for TLS; unknown names fail the load; v26.7.28 added hellochrome_133, hellofirefox_148 and hellosafari_26_3.
Client side only; same list as TLS minus unsafe and hellogolang, which REALITY rejects; empty means chrome.
fromMitm must be the only element when used; values are otherwise not validated (default h2,http/1.1).
Comma-separated hex SHA-256 digests (colons allowed); each must decode to exactly 32 bytes or the load fails.

Format x.y.z with each part < 256; v26.7.28 servers default an unset minClientVer to 26.3.27 and so refuse older Xray clients, while v26.3.27 and v26.9.9 (default commented out again) apply no minimum.

Server mode is chosen by target/dest; it then requires non-empty serverNames, a 32-byte base64url privateKey, non-empty shortIds (each even-length hex up to 16 chars, empty string allowed), xver 0-2, and mldsa65Seed (if set) of 32 bytes different from privateKey.

Without target/dest it is a client: password/publicKey (32-byte base64url) is required, serverNames and shortIds must be empty (use serverName and shortId), shortId is hex up to 16 chars, spiderX must start with '/', mldsa65Verify must be 1952 bytes.
target and dest are the same field (number, host:port, or unix path); target wins when both are set.
password and publicKey are the same client field; password wins when both are set.
Case-insensitive; empty means AsIs; anything else fails the load.
Case-insensitive; empty means none; anything else fails the load.
v26.9.9 fails the load when a freedom outbound sets any addressPortStrategy other than none.

On freedom outbounds v26.9.9 moves a non-AsIs outbound targetStrategy (or else settings.domainStrategy) into sockopt.domainStrategy with a warning, overwriting any sockopt.domainStrategy the config set.
Must be a boolean or a number (true=256, false disables); a string fails the load.

v26.3.27/v26.7.28 accept {tag, transportLayer} (transportLayer true is folded into sockopt.dialerProxy, and a tag together with sockopt.dialerProxy fails the load); v26.9.9 rejects any proxySettings in favour of streamSettings.sockopt.dialerProxy.

From v26.7.28 a VLESS outbound with no stream security and encryption none/empty fails the load unless its address is a private IP or a private/dotless domain (lan, local, localhost, internal, home.arpa, test, ...); v26.7.28 only checks the flat settings.address form (vnext slips through), v26.9.9 checks both forms.

From v26.7.28 a Trojan outbound without stream security fails the load unless its server is a private IP or domain; v26.7.28 only checks the flat settings.address form, v26.9.9 checks servers[0] as well.
A Host entry in headers is moved into host (only if host is empty) with a deprecation warning.
Unlike ws, a Host entry in httpupgrade headers fails the load; use host.
